headline: Highest risk is data leakage/compliance mismatch: Whisper touches audio/speech while the zoomcamp repo is docs-only and no shared execution or filesystem path is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable course repo with no io_surfaces, while agent_b has no clipboard, MCP, stdin/stdout, or filesystem read/write surfaces. Without a bridge, prompt injection from one into the other is not plausible.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the pair, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_b begins parsing agent_a-produced files as instructions, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Disable any future clipboard or MCP bridge between them.
Require provenance labels on any exchanged text.
Review any wrapper that would feed repo content into Whisper.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no runtime surfaces; agent_b touches audio/speech and can only process audio files. There is no documented shared workspace or outbound API path, so leakage is limited to unusual operator wiring rather than default behavior.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory containing sensitive audio and repo artifacts, leakage risk increases.
IF an external wrapper uploads Whisper inputs to a third-party service, reassess upward.
mitigations: Store audio and course materials in separate directories.
Do not mount a shared workspace unless necessary.
Confirm Whisper is run locally with no network egress.
Remove sensitive audio before batch processing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write, network, or execution capabilities documented, and agent_b explicitly lacks filesystem write, git modification, shell, subprocess, and network egress. With no overlapping mutable write surface, there is no capability conflict pathway.
conditions: IF agent_a is wrapped with write or network permissions not shown here, reassess conflict risk.
IF agent_b is granted filesystem write or git access, overlapping mutation could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the current setup.
Avoid granting shared write access to any directory.
Do not enable git automation around either agent.
Document any future permission changes before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a static course repo, not an active generator of authoritative facts, and agent_b is a speech model that processes audio files rather than acting on downstream tasks. The pair lacks documented action-taking authority, so cascading error is limited unless an external orchestrator treats repo text as instructions.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds agent_a outputs into agent_b as authoritative instructions, reassess upward.
IF agent_b is connected to an action-taking workflow, errors could cascade further.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between outputs and any actions.
Treat repo content as reference material only.
Do not auto-execute instructions extracted from either agent.
Log and diff any transformed outputs before use.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly touches audio and speech, which can include personal data, while agent_a is a public data-engineering course repo with no data classes touched. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so the main issue is handling audio data with a non-sensitive public artifact, not a proven compliance breach.
conditions: IF the audio files contain regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance review is required.
IF either agent is deployed under a jurisdiction-specific policy not shown here, reassess.
mitigations: Classify the audio before processing.
Keep regulated audio out of the course repo workspace.
Add a retention note for any transcribed outputs.
Verify local-only processing for Whisper.
